key_insight: A 9-qubit superconducting quantum processor can digitally emulate 3D Ising criticality on a Platonic lattice and recover near-theory critical exponents.
engineering_relevance: This demonstrates a path to studying higher-dimensional critical phenomena on near-term quantum hardware with nontrivial connectivity and limited qubit counts.
method: Extended VQE with a phase-based loss function prepares low-energy states.
4 lowest eigenenergies are read out via Fourier-transform analysis and numerical fitting.
3D Ising model is encoded on an 8-qubit cubic Platonic lattice within a 9-qubit processor.
evidence_signal: The extracted energies agree with exact diagonalization to within +/- 0.001, yielding Delta_epsilon = 1.5850 and nu = 0.7067.
watch_item: The approach depends on specialized lattice encoding and high spectral resolution, so scaling beyond small systems may be challenging.
paper_title: 3D Ising criticality with Platonic lattice superconducting qubits
